items.text: Theorem. A sheaf $F$ on $\mathrm{Sch}/S$ is a scheme iff there exist subsheaves $F_i\subset F$ with: (a) $F_i\to F$ open immersions; (b) $\sup_iF_i=F$; (c) each $F_i$ is a scheme over $S$.
Corollary. (c) may be replaced by (c$'$): each $F_i$ is representable by an affine scheme (for $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$: a representable functor on $k$-algebras).
(b) in algebra: each $a\in F(k')$ lies locally in some $F_i$: there are $f_\alpha\in k'$ generating the unit ideal and $i(\alpha)$ with $a|_{k'_{f_\alpha}}\in F_{i(\alpha)}(k'_{f_\alpha})$.
U'=S'\setminus V(J),\quad S'=\operatorname{Spec}k':\qquad U'(B)=\{\,u\colon k'\to B : u(J)B=B\,\}
$J=(g_\lambda)$: $u(g_\lambda)$ generate the unit ideal of $B$. Open immersions make sense for functors on algebras.
